result.summary: Fixed cancellation-2. In zendriver/core/tab.py, a new private helper `_wait_for(aw, timeout)` built on asyncio.wait replaces the four Q2 asyncio.wait_for bounds: _poll_with_timeout (used by find, select, find_all, select_all, wait_for and Tab.__call__), Tab.xpath, and in zendriver/core/cloudflare.py cf_wait_for_interactive_challenge and the verify_cf click phase. The helper runs the attempt with ensure_future and waits on it with asyncio.wait({task}, timeout). If the caller is cancelled, it cancels the attempt, waits for it to finish and re-raises the CancelledError, even when the attempt finished in the same loop iteration (CPython gh-86296). On timeout it cancels the attempt, waits for it and raises asyncio.TimeoutError, or the attempt's own non-cancel exception, as wait_for does. A done callback reads the attempt's result so asyncio never logs 'exception was never retrieved'. The call sites are changed only from asyncio.wait_for to _wait_for, so the TimeoutError messages, xpath's [], cf_is_interactive_challenge_present's False, the one-shot behaviour for timeout <= 0 and the 0.5 s grace stay as they were. Browser._stop, and the wait_for calls that already existed before the bug hunt (Tab.get navigate, wait_for_ready_state, line ~1169), were left alone. There are no public signature changes and the patch is one commit on top of 8ae752b. HEAD is now detached.

result.notes:
Residual risks and behaviour notes:
(1) On Python 3.12 and later, the helper now runs the attempt in its own task, where wait_for ran it inline. As a result, when the caller is cancelled and the attempt's cleanup raises a different exception, the caller now gets CancelledError instead of that exception. That matches what 3.10/3.11 wait_for already did, and it is what a canceller expects. The error is also retrieved, so nothing is logged.
(2) If the bound runs out and the attempt swallows its cancellation and returns a value, the helper raises TimeoutError. 3.10 wait_for does the same; 3.12+ wait_for returned the value. If the attempt instead raises a non-cancel exception while it is being cancelled, that exception propagates, the same as wait_for on every version.
(3) As with wait_for, the helper waits for the cancelled attempt to finish. An attempt that ignores its cancellation would therefore still block the caller. This is unchanged.
(4) Out of scope and unchanged: three asyncio.wait_for calls that existed before the bug hunt keep the gh-86296 window on 3.10/3.11. They are Tab.wait_for_ready_state (line ~1450), Tab.get's navigate bound (~599) and the bound at ~1169. Browser._stop's wait_for was left alone as instructed. Converting them to _wait_for would be a one-word change if wanted later.
(5) The cancellation-1 wedge (Q2 timeout plus Q12 rollback behind a dialog) is a separate finding and is not addressed here.
(6) The new tests are deterministic: the answer future is resolved and task.cancel() is called in the same loop iteration, and every wait has a positive outer safety-net timeout. The retrieval test filters caplog on a unique message ('the cancelled attempt failed'), so unrelated 'never retrieved' logs from other tests cannot make it fail.

result.summary:
One commit on top of ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh (8ae752b), all in zendriver/core/connection.py.

(1) cancellation-1: in `_register_handlers`, the `except CancelledError` branch now looks for the cancelled enable in self.mapper. It matches by identity of the cdp generator (`t.__cdp_obj__ is enable`), so a pending manual X.enable with the same method name is not mistaken for it. A written enable stays in the mapper until Chrome answers; one that never left is popped. When the enable never left, the domain is rolled back as before. When it was written, the domain stays enabled, so later sends no longer queue a second enable behind the first, and the dialog can be dismissed again. To close the gap the reviewer flagged, `_expect_enable_response()` puts a stand-in Transaction under the same id. Its done-callback removes the domain from enabled_domains if the browser rejects the enable, or if the stand-in is failed by a close, detach or receive error. Without it, a written enable that Chrome later rejected would stay marked enabled and never be retried.

(2) connection-2, lifecycle-3, connection-3: send() wraps `_register_handlers`, the detached check and `_send_transaction` in try/finally with a `sent` flag.
- (a) If the tx is already done after `_register_handlers` (failed by a receive error, close or detach), send() does not transmit it. It raises that failure through the existing `await tx` path, so ProtocolException still gets its command and params annotation.
- (b) If send() leaves without transmitting (exception, cancellation, detached session, or a failed or cancelled write), the finally block pops the tx from the mapper. It also calls `tx.exception()` if the tx was failed meanwhile, which marks the failure as retrieved.
- (c) `_update_manual_domain` now returns the module it added to manually_enabled_domains. The finally block removes that entry again when the manual X.enable never left. An entry made by an earlier call is kept.

While verifying lifecycle-3 with the reviewer's concurrent-stop probe, I found a second path that the listed windows did not cover. The close fails the pending Browser.close tx while `websocket.send()` is still in progress, and then the write itself raises ConnectionClosed. send() raises the write error, so nobody retrieves the tx's own failure. The `tx.exception()` call above covers it. Before: 4 of 6 runs logged the warning on 3.13. After: 0 of 6.

(3) connection-1: a NamedTuple sentinel `_ReceiveError(exception, pending)`. On an unexpected receive error, the browser listener puts it into each attached session's `_inbox`, carrying the ids that session had in its mapper at that moment. It falls back to `_fail_pending_transactions` when a session has no inbox. When the session's `_receive_message` reaches the sentinel, the replies queued ahead of it have already been dispatched. It then fails only the listed ids still in its mapper and returns None, so listener_loop itself is unchanged. Commands sent after the error, which a revived reader answers, are not affected.

Verification:
- Reviewer probes on 3.10 and 3.13:
  - probe_fake_dialog_wedge: 'dismiss: OK', methods ['Log.enable','Page.handleJavaScriptDialog']
  - probe_routed_then_fail: 'send returned 2'
  - probe_failed_then_sent2: only ['Page.enable','Page.enable'] reach the browser
  - probe_manual_enable_cancel: 'Overlay.enable ever sent: True', manually_enabled_domains []
- Real-Chromium dialog probes:
  - probe_dialog_recover log/select on 3.13 and runtime/select on 3.10: 'handleJavaScriptDialog OK after 0.00s', and the next select finds #hello
  - probe_expect_dialog on 3.13: OK
- Reviewer stress harnesses: stress_domains.py (6 seeds with NOANS=0, 3 seeds default) and stress.py (4 seeds), 0 problems on both Pythons.
- `bash scripts/format.sh` and `bash scripts/lint.sh` are clean (ruff, ruff format, mypy).

result.notes:
Residual risks and judgement calls:

1. Semantic change from cancellation-1: a cancelled, written enable that the browser never answers now stays marked enabled indefinitely, until a reply, a close, detach or receive error, or the domain going stale. Real Chrome always answers or the session dies, and the reviewer's stress_domains with the default never-answered rate still reported 0 problems.

2. The stand-in replaces the cancelled tx under the same id. A late rejection of an old enable can remove a domain that was meanwhile re-enabled successfully. The cost is one redundant re-enable on the next send.

3. "Written" means `_send_transaction` returned. If websockets' send() is cancelled after handing the frame to the transport (while draining), the enable is treated as not sent and is re-sent once. This is harmless except in the dialog case, where it could stall once more.

4. Undoing a never-sent manual X.enable removes X from manually_enabled_domains, but does not put X back into enabled_domains when it was auto-enabled before. The next send just re-enables it (redundant enable, no functional loss).

5. The sentinel fails the session ids pending at the time of the error. A reply for one of them that a revived reader routes in later is dropped, the same as before.

6. `_send_oneshot` still has the 'failed meanwhile, then the write fails' window. It is only used by `_prepare_headless` and `_prepare_expert`, and was left out of scope.

7. One-off failure of test_select_with_include_frames_clicks_element_in_cross_site_frame in the first 3.13 full run. I did not capture its traceback. It did not recur in 2 more full runs and 8 targeted loops, and nothing in this diff runs on the normal send path. Every changed branch needs a cancellation, a receive error or a send that never left. Most likely a load flake of the cross-site iframe click.

8. The lifecycle-3 fix went slightly beyond the listed windows: `tx.exception()` in send()'s cleanup covers a close that fails the tx and then its write. The new test test_close_during_a_failing_write_leaves_no_unretrieved_failure reproduces the exact 'Transaction exception was never retrieved' for that case.

9. The main checkout and branch ccr-9a8a26e1-b0l7bh are untouched (still 8ae752b). The worktree is detached at e7d5a85. Scratch scripts and logs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/followup/U1/.
